scenario_scope: Primary-source intake of elizaOS, Nous Research Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw as external implementation comparators for modular agent runtimes, governed tool use, procedural memory, session identity, evidence capture, and runtime composition.

cases.decision_rationale: elizaOS supplies a concrete modular runtime and scenario-runner comparator, while runtime authority, evidence qualification, and promotion already have explicit owners in the existing book.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical core-runtime, scenario-runner, security, and sandbox documentation
separate implemented project surfaces from the shared ChatGPT review's unverified diagnoses
evidence_transition_preconditions: run a claim-specific local or independently reviewed comparison
retain exact version, configuration, failures, costs, and boundary conditions
promotion_blockers: no local elizaOS execution or scenario reproduction
no independent security or performance assessment
non_claims: does not import reported project behavior into the ASI Stack
does not establish runtime safety, readiness, or state of the art
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

cases.decision_rationale: Hermes Agent provides a concrete skill-learning, persistent-memory, session-search, approval, and isolation comparator; those mechanisms fit established memory and runtime owners rather than a standalone product chapter.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical skills, memory, security, and architecture documentation
distinguish agent-authored procedures from validated or promoted capabilities
evidence_transition_preconditions: execute a claim-specific procedure-learning or memory-integrity comparison
measure proposal quality, regression, rollback, poisoning, and human-review costs
promotion_blockers: no reproduced learning, memory, security, or utility result
non_claims: does not equate skill mutation with safe self-improvement
does not establish memory correctness or command safety
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

cases.decision_rationale: OpenClaw supplies concrete gateway, session, ACP harness, policy, audit, and governed self-learning surfaces. It complements rather than duplicates the existing Claw-SWE-Bench evaluation source and fits four established lifecycle owners.
required_before_drafting: review the official repository at a pinned commit
review canonical gateway, agent-loop, ACP, sandbox-policy, memory, and self-learning documentation
keep the OpenClaw implementation source distinct from the Claw-SWE-Bench benchmark source
evidence_transition_preconditions: run a version-pinned claim-specific gateway, session, policy, or learning comparison
retain failures, policy configuration, identity joins, costs, and unresolved residuals
promotion_blockers: no reproduced security, reliability, learning, or benchmark result
non_claims: does not transfer Claw-SWE-Bench results to OpenClaw or the ASI Stack
does not establish ACP harness confinement or end-to-end authority correctness
does not justify a new paper-shaped chapter

validation_boundary: Records a primary-source existing-owner routing decision for three public software projects. It does not reproduce the projects, validate their documentation, import their reported results, establish novelty, or move any claim support state.
non_claims: does not create a new chapter
does not add a Lean proof result
does not authorize deployment, release, or claim promotion
